purpose: How a plating bench decides which gold system a given job must run — which chemistry family and named commercial product, which strike, build and colour roles, which support baths underneath, and which jobs belong to another process entirely — by screening the job's substrate, geometry, wear class, colour target, forming order, skin-contact status and claim class against what each family physically deposits and what obligation class the shop must satisfy to be allowed to run it.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the bench buys commercial plating chemistry and runs each product per its own technical data sheet; nothing here is formulated from raw chemicals

operating windows, replenisher schedules and analysis targets belong to the chosen product's data sheet and to the shop's own logged runs; this knowledge base teaches what each family does and how to choose between them, not what numbers to dial in

the shop operates under some jurisdiction's workplace, hazmat, waste-discharge and jewellery-marking rules; every regulated item here is a class to verify locally and currently, never a threshold asserted from memory
handbook-class figures quoted from the in-repo process corpus are referenced as handbook-class comparisons that set expectations; where the corpus records something as unknown it stays unknown here
exclusions: bath setpoints and operating windows (temperature, pH, gold concentration, current density, time) — these come from the specific product's technical data sheet, never from this knowledge base

keeping a selected bath inside its window: what each parameter does to the deposit in service, drift signatures, analysis method classes (titration, Hull cell, coupon plus XRF, supplier lab) and replenishment discipline — the sibling bath analysis and control knowledge base

contamination control, drag-in and drag-out management, filtration and carbon treatment, bath aging, regenerate-versus-replace economics and gold recovery from spent solutions and rinses — the sibling contamination and lifecycle knowledge base
surface preparation and rinse execution — cleaning, pickling, activation and water-break testing belong to the surface preparation specialist
racking, current calculation, run sequencing and hands-on plating execution — the process execution specialist

test methods and acceptance criteria for thickness, adhesion, porosity and colour measurement — the quality and finish specialist; this knowledge base only consumes their results as a selection sign-off
any do-it-yourself bath formulation from raw salts, and any improvised cyanide handling procedure; cyanide content here is obligation-class guidance pointing at formal training and jurisdiction rules
physical vapour deposition and other vacuum coating work — named only as an out-of-scope alternative class for referral, never specified or selected here
personalised legal, medical or financial advice; nickel-allergy, chemical-exposure and compliance questions route to current jurisdiction rules and to appropriate professional care
asserted numeric thresholds for regulated terms such as gold plated, vermeil, gold filled, rolled gold, nickel release and discharge limits — named as obligation classes to verify locally
prices, gold market values, wear-life guarantees and thickness promises

competency_questions.question: Which gold chemistry family should this job run, and what specifically disqualifies the other families?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the four family nodes each state what they deposit, what they cost the shop and what disqualifies them, and JOB_SPEC_INTAKE supplies the profile they are screened against

competency_questions.question: What must this shop be able to prove about itself before it is allowed to run a cyanide-bearing gold bath at all, and what is the absolute line around acids?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HAZARD_CLASS_READINESS names the obligation classes per family, states that cyanide-bearing and acid solutions are never mixed, co-stored or co-drained, and produces a written per-family readiness verdict verified against jurisdiction rules

competency_questions.question: Where do the operating numbers for the bath I picked actually come from, and what do I do when a forum recipe or a remembered figure contradicts them?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TDS_PRIMACY establishes that selection ends at a named commercial product whose data sheet governs its window, matching strike, replenisher and anode class, with handbook ranges explaining mechanism rather than replacing the sheet

competency_questions.question: Do I need a separate gold strike, or can I plate straight into the build bath?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GOLD_STRIKE_ROLE explains immersion-deposit suppression, adhesion and the strike's sacrificial protection of the build bath, and states the system-compatibility rule between strike and build

competency_questions.question: How many gold tanks does this finish really need — strike, build, colour flash — and what does each one cost me just to keep alive between jobs?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STRIKE_COLOR_BUILD_STACK assigns the three bath roles to the job and GOLD_INVENTORY_AND_BATH_LIFE gives the standing-cost mechanism of each additional system

competency_questions.question: How do I get a rose, green or paler yellow tone, and what does that do to the karat I can honestly describe?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COLOR_KARAT_ALLOYING names which co-deposited metals shift hue which way, explains that an alloyed coating's effective karat is a recipe property, and COLOR_TARGET_SPEC fixes the reference the result is judged against

competency_questions.question: What underplate does this substrate need, and which support bath class supplies it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SUPPORT_BATH_CLASSES gives the nickel, copper, palladium and Wood's-class strike options with what each buys, and SUBSTRATE_COMPATIBILITY gives the stack each substrate class demands

competency_questions.question: The piece is worn against skin and the customer raises a nickel concern — how does that change the stack, and what am I allowed to tell them?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NICKEL_FREE_SELECTION treats nickel release as an obligation class to verify in the current jurisdiction, gives the non-nickel barrier alternatives as classes, and routes allergy questions to professional care rather than to shop reassurance

competency_questions.question: The part has to be bent, riveted or stone-set after plating — which families survive that and which crack?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FORM_ORDER_DUCTILITY ranks the families and underplate classes by formability, states that form-first is the default, and names what plate-then-form spends in wear resistance

competency_questions.question: The piece is a hollow filigree pendant, a bore or a tangled chain — will a rack gold bath even reach those surfaces, or do I need the no-rectifier class?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EFFICIENCY_AND_RATE_CLASS explains throwing power as a geometry limit and ELECTROLESS_IMMERSION_CLASS gives the current-free uniformity answer together with its hard thickness ceiling

competency_questions.question: How hard a life will this piece have, and what wear class and thickness class does that make honest to offer?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WEAR_CLASS_LADDER maps service duty onto a wear class and treats coating thickness classes as published standard classes to verify, producing a disclosed wear expectation rather than a life guarantee

competency_questions.question: Can I call the finished piece gold plated or vermeil, and does the system I chose actually support that claim?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DISCLOSURE_AND_MARKING_CLASS treats the claim terms as obligation classes to verify locally, ties the claim back to substrate and thickness class, and states that plated work is never represented as solid gold

competency_questions.question: When is this job not an electroplating job at all, and how do I say so without simply losing the customer?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PVD_OUT_OF_SCOPE_BOUNDARY names vacuum coating as an alternative class for referral and gives the triage that turns an unwinnable job into an honest referral or refusal

competency_questions.question: How do I prove the chosen system works before the customer's piece goes in, and what has to be written down so the next run and the bath-maintenance side can reproduce it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TRIAL_PANEL_QUALIFICATION defines the coupon set and the four selection-level checks it must pass, and SELECTION_DOSSIER lists the record contents handed off to bath maintenance including accepted residual risks

glossary.definition: A deliberately lean gold bath, rich in complexant relative to its gold content, run first and briefly to lay down a thin high-adhesion gold layer; it suppresses spontaneous immersion deposition on less-noble surfaces and absorbs drag-in that would otherwise reach the build bath. It is sacrificial by design and is remade rather than nursed when it goes off.

The thickness-carrying gold bath: the tank where ampere-minutes become microns and therefore where wear life is actually bought. Distinct in composition and purpose from both the strike that precedes it and any colour flash that follows it.

A thin final gold coat, usually lean and intentionally alloyed, whose job is hue rather than thickness. It sits over a build layer or a bright underplate, is measured in fractions of a micron, and must never be mistaken for the wear layer.

Soft gold is a near-pure, ductile 24k-class deposit that burnishes and scratches easily; hard gold is a grain-refined deposit carrying a small co-deposited hardener and inclusions, roughly two to three times harder by the handbook-class figures in the process corpus, and correspondingly brittle. The choice is a wear-versus-formability decision, not a quality ranking.

Gold plating out of solution spontaneously because the surface metal is less noble and gives up electrons for it — no rectifier involved. It is self-limiting once gold covers the surface, and when it happens unintentionally under a plating bath it is the classic cause of a coating with no adhesion.

The fraction of the current passed that actually becomes deposited metal rather than gas. It is a family-level property that sets how long a target thickness takes: the process corpus records the alkaline cyanide family as very high and the acid hardened family as far lower, which shows up on the bench as rack occupancy, not as an electricity bill.

A bath's ability to deposit evenly into recesses, bores and shielded areas where current distribution is poor. Where throwing power runs out, more current burns edges instead of filling recesses, and the answer is a different process class rather than a bigger rectifier.

The plated layer between the customer's metal and the gold — most often a nickel class, sometimes copper, palladium or a Wood's-class strike. It blocks base-metal diffusion into thin gold, blocks corrosion through coating pores, and levels the surface so a thin gold layer looks and behaves like more than it is.

The supplier's document for a specific commercial product: its operating window, its matching strike and replenisher, its anode and filtration classes and its declared application envelope. In this trade it is the authority for setpoints; handbook ranges explain what those setpoints do but never replace the sheet.

The regulated vocabulary attached to a finished piece — gold plated, vermeil, gold filled, rolled gold — each of which carries substrate, process and thickness requirements set by the market's rules. They are classes to verify currently in your jurisdiction, and a plated piece is never described as solid gold.

nodes.definition: Before any bath is named, write down what the finished piece has to be: the substrate metal and whatever alloy, solder and previous coating history it carries, the geometry class (flat rack-friendly faces versus bores, hollows, chain and filigree), the service duty the piece will actually see, the colour the customer expects and the reference it will be judged against, whether the metal is formed before or after plating, whether the item touches skin or food, which market's marking rules apply, and the batch size and turnaround. This profile is the input every later choice is scored against. Unknowns are recorded as unknowns rather than smoothed over — 'the customer thinks it is stainless' is a different input from a verified substrate — because a guessed substrate is the most common root cause of a batch that has to be stripped and started again.

included: substrate, geometry, duty, colour, forming order, contact class, market and volume capture
explicit marking of unverified claims as unknown
the profile as the screening input for every family decision
excluded: cleaning and preparation method choice
run parameters and racking
quoting or pricing the job

pros.claim: It forces the disqualifying constraints into view before any money is spent on chemistry
pros.example: a customer's casual 'just gold plate these' turns out to describe spring-steel clips that get bent after plating, which eliminates hardened acid gold on the spot

cons.claim: Intake costs bench time and customers frequently cannot answer the questions that matter most
cons.example: an heirloom arrives with unknown solder alloys and an unknown previous coating, so the profile stays partly unknown and the job has to carry a stated risk instead of a promise

failure_modes: accepting the customer's word on the substrate as if it were verified
leaving the wear class unstated so the bench silently defaults to a decorative flash
never asking whether the piece is formed or set after plating
acceptance_tests: the brief records substrate (marked verified or unverified), geometry class, wear class, colour reference, forming order, skin or food contact, target market and batch size, with every unknown explicitly labelled as unknown
revisit_triggers: the customer changes the item, its finish expectation or its intended use
substrate verification contradicts what intake recorded

base.update_signal: a pattern of jobs failing for a requirement the intake form never asked about

nodes.definition: Selection ends at a named commercial product, not at a chemistry class: 'acid hardened gold' is a family, while 'this supplier's cobalt-hardened acid gold, this revision of the sheet' is what the bench actually runs. The technical data sheet is the authority for that product's operating window, its matching strike and replenisher, its anode and filtration classes and the applications the supplier will stand behind; handbook ranges and the process corpus behind this knowledge base explain what those numbers do, they do not replace them. Three consequences follow on the bench: obtain and file the technical and safety data sheets before the drum arrives, never mix one supplier's strike or replenisher into another supplier's build bath unless both sheets say it is allowed, and never substitute a forum recipe or a remembered figure for the sheet. Nothing here is formulated from raw chemicals.

included: product-level rather than family-level selection
obtaining and filing the technical and safety data sheets
system compatibility of strike, replenisher, anode and filtration as the sheet declares them
supplier technical support and lab service as a named class
excluded: the setpoints themselves and their day-to-day control
any formulation from raw salts
analysis method execution

pros.claim: It makes every later parameter argument resolvable by document instead of by memory or seniority
pros.example: a dispute about a drifting colour is settled by reading the sheet's hardener and pH window rather than by someone dosing 'a bit more' of the hardener

cons.claim: It ties the bench to one supplier's system and to that system's availability
cons.example: a discontinued colour flash forces a full re-qualification because the replacement product's window and tone are never quite identical

failure_modes: buying chemistry on price with no sheet in hand
mixing strikes, replenishers or additives across supplier systems
treating a published handbook range as if it were this product's window
acceptance_tests: every bath in the plan names a specific commercial product with its current technical and safety data sheets on file, and the compatible strike, replenisher and anode class are identified from that sheet rather than assumed
revisit_triggers: the supplier reformulates, renames or discontinues the product
a sheet revision changes the window, the compatible components or the declared application envelope

base.update_signal: a supplier sheet revision, a product discontinuation, or a supplier statement about cross-system compatibility

nodes.definition: Decide what the shop is equipped and permitted to run before deciding what it would like to run. Each family carries an obligation class: cyanide-bearing golds and strikes demand formal training, secure and segregated storage, labelling, dedicated ventilation, spill and emergency readiness, and licensing arrangements that vary by jurisdiction; acid systems carry their own storage, ventilation and personal protective equipment duties; sulfite systems shed the cyanide obligations but re-import serious hazmat duties whenever a hardened variant carries an arsenic- or thallium-class dopant. One line is absolute and reappears in the tank layout, the storage plan and the drain plan alike: cyanide-bearing solutions and acids are never mixed, never stored together and never share a drain, because acidifying a cyanide solution liberates lethal gas. Note that an acid gold bath built on a cyanide complex is still a cyanide-bearing solution for storage, segregation and waste purposes. The output is a written per-family verdict — available, available with conditions, or not available to this shop — with every item verified against the jurisdiction's workplace and hazmat rules and against formal training, never improvised.

included: obligation classes per chemistry family
physical and procedural segregation of cyanide-bearing and acid tanks, stores and drains
training, labelling, ventilation, protective equipment and emergency readiness as classes
jurisdiction verification and the written readiness verdict
excluded: the handling procedures themselves, which belong to formal training and the safety specialist
waste treatment and destruction methods, which belong to the lifecycle knowledge base
exposure limits and monitoring thresholds stated as numbers

pros.claim: It removes unrunnable options while they are still free to remove
pros.example: a bench with no ventilated, lockable, segregated zone learns that the cyanide families are out at the gate rather than after a drum of gold salt has been delivered

cons.claim: The readiness bar can push a shop toward a chemistry that is technically worse for the job in hand
cons.example: choosing a sulfite system for a formable piece purely because the cyanide obligations are out of reach, and then paying for it in shorter bath life and tighter drag-in sensitivity

failure_modes: treating safety as a paragraph appended after the chemistry has already been chosen
assuming a neighbouring shop's permissions, training or ventilation apply to yours
improvising a cyanide handling or neutralisation step from an internet video
laying out tanks so an acid drip tray can reach a cyanide-bearing sump
acceptance_tests: a dated written verdict exists per family citing training status, secure storage, tank and drain segregation, ventilation, protective equipment, emergency readiness and the jurisdiction check, and no family is shortlisted whose verdict is not available or available with conditions that are actually in place
revisit_triggers: training lapses, or the trained operator leaves
ventilation, storage or drainage in the room changes
jurisdiction rules or licensing arrangements change
a new chemistry family is proposed for the bench

base.update_signal: a change in the shop's training, storage, ventilation or licensing status, or a change in the jurisdiction's workplace and hazmat rules

nodes.definition: Translate how the piece will live into a wear class, because that is what drives the hardness and thickness demand and therefore the family. An earring post worn twice a year, a pendant that hangs still, a bracelet that rubs a desk edge, a ring shank that grinds against a second ring and a watch case are five different duties. The coating classes the corpus records run from flash — a fraction of a micron, decorative, months rather than years of wear life — through the plated and micron-plating classes up to the heavy-wear class used on rings and bracelets, and those class names come from published standards to be verified rather than invented. The expert output is a wear class plus the plain-language wear expectation that goes with it, written down before any thickness is promised, because a flash coating on a ring shank is not a defect: it is a mis-selection that the customer will blame on the plater.

included: mapping service duty onto a wear class
coating thickness classes treated as published standard classes to verify
the disclosed wear expectation that accompanies the class
excluded: measuring achieved thickness, which is the quality specialist's method class
guaranteeing a service life in years
setting current and time to reach a thickness

pros.claim: It converts a vague 'make it last' into a class that families can actually be screened against
pros.example: assigning a ring shank to the heavy-wear class immediately rules out an immersion-gold flash as the final finish, before anyone argues about colour

cons.claim: A wear class is a prediction about a person's habits and it can be wrong in both directions
cons.example: a 'gentle wear' pendant that ends up on a working jeweller's own bench chain wears like a bracelet and returns early

failure_modes: quoting a thickness class from marketing copy rather than from the standard it claims to follow
promising a number of years of wear life
letting price pressure silently downgrade the class after the customer agreed to it
acceptance_tests: each item carries a recorded wear class and a plain-language wear expectation that was disclosed to the customer before work started, with the thickness class named as a standard class rather than as a promise
revisit_triggers: wear complaints or returns cluster on one product line
the customer describes a use that differs from what intake captured

base.update_signal: field wear feedback or returns data that contradicts the class assigned at selection

nodes.definition: Pin the colour before choosing the bath that has to hit it. Gold colour is judged by comparison, never by adjectives: the trade's colour classes — the Swiss and NIHS 1N, 2N and 3N class names the corpus records — physical reference plaques, a retained master sample from a previous accepted run, or instrumented colour measurement in larger shops all serve as references, while 'a rich yellow' serves as nothing. The specification also states the conditions the comparison happens under, because the same coating reads differently against a different background, under a different lamp and at a different polish state. Finally it says whether the target is the pure 24k-class tone a fine-gold bath gives on its own or an alloyed hue that only a colour bath can produce, since those are different mechanisms with different stability, and the underplate's brightness reads straight through a thin gold layer.

included: colour class names, reference plaques and retained masters as the comparison basis
stated viewing conditions
distinguishing a pure-gold tone from an alloyed hue at specification time
excluded: colour measurement instrumentation and its procedure
holding colour run to run through bath control, which is the maintenance knowledge base
final acceptance judgement, which is the quality specialist's

pros.claim: A fixed reference turns colour from an argument into a comparison
pros.example: a customer's 'it looks too brassy' is settled against the agreed plaque under the agreed light instead of against two people's memories

cons.claim: References age and the eye is context-dependent, so the basis itself can drift
cons.example: a retained master that has tarnished slightly in a drawer makes a correct new batch look wrong and sends the bench chasing a fault that is not there

failure_modes: agreeing colour verbally and discovering the disagreement at delivery
comparing under bench lighting the customer will never see the piece in
ignoring that a bright or dull underplate changes the perceived colour of a thin gold coat
acceptance_tests: an agreed colour reference — class name, plaque or retained master — and its viewing conditions are recorded before any qualification coupon is plated
revisit_triggers: the reference plaque or retained master is replaced or has visibly aged
the customer supplies a new sample to match

base.update_signal: a colour dispute that the existing reference could not settle, or a new reference standard adopted by the shop

nodes.definition: The reference family every alternative is benchmarked against: gold carried as the very stable aurocyanide complex with an excess of free cyanide, run strongly alkaline and hot, depositing near-pure 24k-class soft gold at very high cathode efficiency according to the published chemistry in the process corpus. Its selection strengths are the richest standard yellow, the most ductile gold deposit available and therefore the family to reach for when the metal is formed or gently bent after plating, high efficiency so microns arrive quickly, and the strongest strikes for awkward or mixed-metal surfaces. Its selection liabilities are two and they are both structural: the top hazard tier, because free cyanide combined with an alkalinity floor below which lethal gas evolves brings the whole obligation class with it; and softness in service, because an unhardened 24k coat burnishes and scratches on daily-wear surfaces. Its lean, deliberately alloyed flash variants are the classic route to tuned decorative hues.

included: what the family deposits and why it is the benchmark
its strike, build and colour-variant roles
the hazard tier and what it costs to be allowed to run it
the wear classes its softness disqualifies it from
excluded: its operating setpoints, which belong to the product sheet
carbonate build-up and contamination management in service, which belong to the lifecycle knowledge base
cyanide handling procedure, which belongs to formal training

pros.claim: It offers ductility and colour depth no other electrodeposited gold matches, plus the strongest activation strikes
pros.example: an antique repair with mixed solder joints and a fine-gold colour target is a job where a cyanide strike grips what other strikes will not and the soft build takes gentle reshaping afterwards

cons.claim: It is the most expensive family to be permitted to run, entirely independent of the gold it deposits
cons.example: segregated secure storage, dedicated ventilation, emergency readiness, training and licensing all exist before the first gram of gold is deposited, which many small benches cannot justify for occasional work

failure_modes: shortlisting the family in a shop whose readiness verdict does not permit it
promising ring-grade scratch resistance from an unhardened soft deposit
using the lean colour flash variant as if it were a thickness builder
acceptance_tests: any selection of this family cites the readiness verdict that permits it, names the commercial product with its sheet on file, and pairs a soft-gold choice with an explicit wear-class justification
revisit_triggers: the shop's cyanide readiness verdict changes in either direction
the job's wear class rises above what an unhardened deposit can honestly serve

base.update_signal: corpus or supplier evidence that changes this family's role boundaries, or a change in the shop's readiness state

nodes.definition: The wear family: the same aurocyanide complex, this time in an acidic citrate- or phosphate-buffered electrolyte carrying a small cobalt or nickel addition that co-deposits at fractions of a percent along with carbon and polymer inclusions, refining the grain and lifting hardness roughly two to three times over pure soft gold — the corpus records handbook-class figures of about sixty to ninety on the Vickers scale for soft gold against roughly one hundred and thirty to two hundred for hardened acid gold. It plates bright as deposited, which saves post-buffing, and it is the industry's continuous strip and connector chemistry, so it scales well. Its costs are equally structural: the deposit is brittle and microcracks if the part is formed afterwards, cathode efficiency is far lower than the alkaline family so each micron takes markedly longer, its tone depends on the hardener level and the operating conditions and therefore drifts when they drift, and its acidity attacks bare steel so it demands a sound barrier underneath. It remains a cyanide-bearing solution despite the acid pH, and is stored, segregated and waste-handled as one.

included: the hardening mechanism and the wear payoff it buys
brightness as deposited and suitability for continuous and connector-style work
brittleness, low efficiency, hardener-dependent tone and substrate attack as selection costs
its status as a cyanide-bearing solution for storage, segregation and waste
excluded: setpoints and hardener concentration control
hardener analysis method classes
wear and adhesion test execution

pros.claim: It is the common electroplated gold that survives ring-grade abrasion without needing a protective topcoat
pros.example: a signet ring shank that would burnish through a soft 24k coat within weeks holds a hardened deposit far longer under the same daily contact

cons.claim: Its brittleness makes it incompatible with any post-plate forming, and the cracks it opens expose the barrier and base metal
cons.example: bending plated wire into a ring after plating crazes the gold at the bend radius and opens both a corrosion path and a skin-contact exposure path through to the nickel underneath

failure_modes: assuming that acid pH means the bath is not a cyanide-bearing solution for storage and waste purposes
letting the hardener level drift and then blaming the colour change on the customer's lighting
plating over an inadequate barrier so the acid electrolyte reaches the steel underneath
acceptance_tests: a selection of this family records the wear class it serves, the barrier it requires, the forming order it forbids, and an explicit statement that the bath is handled as cyanide-bearing
revisit_triggers: the job acquires a post-plate forming, riveting or setting step
colour reproducibility complaints appear across batches

base.update_signal: supplier or corpus evidence revising the hardness, efficiency or brittleness expectations for hardened acid golds

nodes.definition: Between the strongly alkaline and the frankly acid systems sits a near-neutral class, and the reason to know it is compatibility rather than deposit glamour: a bath's pH is an attack vector on whatever is already on the part. An acid gold electrolyte attacks bare steel and can dull or dissolve sensitive underlayers and assembled components, while a strongly alkaline cyanide bath is aggressive to other things. Near-neutral gold baths — neutral cyanide-complex golds in electronics practice, and the mixed sulfite-thiosulfate variant the corpus records, which exploits the stronger thiosulfate complex to run near neutral with better shelf stability at the price of sulfur co-deposition risk — exist to plate onto substrates and assemblies that either pH extreme would damage. Treat this as a compatibility class to look for in a supplier catalogue when pH is the actual problem, and treat its window, deposit hardness and colour as strictly product-sheet and qualification territory.

included: pH as a substrate and assembly compatibility axis
when to go looking for a near-neutral product
the near-neutral sulfite-thiosulfate variant as the corpus records it
excluded: any asserted pH window, hardness or colour figure for the class
the class's control and stabiliser regime
hazard classification shortcuts based on pH

pros.claim: It solves the jobs where the chosen family's pH, rather than its deposit, is the problem
pros.example: a mixed assembly holding a component that an acid citrate electrolyte would etch is a compatibility question that no amount of current or hardener tuning answers

cons.claim: It is a thinner and more supplier-specific class with much less shop folklore behind it
cons.example: fewer products and fewer peers who have run them means the qualification effort per job is higher and there is nobody to ask when a coupon comes out wrong

failure_modes: assuming that near-neutral means low-hazard when a neutral cyanide-complex bath is still cyanide-bearing
adopting the class on a catalogue description without qualifying colour and wear
using it to avoid solving an underlying barrier or preparation problem
acceptance_tests: a near-neutral selection states which pH incompatibility it exists to solve, names the product and sheet, and carries its own hazard classification rather than inheriting an assumption from its pH
revisit_triggers: the assembly or substrate that motivated the pH choice changes
the supplier's near-neutral product line changes or is withdrawn

base.update_signal: supplier documentation or corpus evidence that sharpens what the near-neutral class actually offers on jewellery substrates

nodes.definition: The non-cyanide route: gold carried as a sulfite complex in a mildly alkaline electrolyte with an excess of free sulfite and proprietary organic stabilisers. The corpus is blunt about the underlying trade — the sulfite complex is far weaker than aurocyanide, so the gold is thermodynamically prone to disproportionation and the bath will drop metallic gold onto tank walls, heaters and dust nuclei unless it is held alkaline with excess sulfite plus stabilisers, and it dies in fewer metal turnovers than a cyanide bath. What it buys is genuine: no cyanide obligation class, a high-purity low-stress ductile 24k-class deposit that is the most post-formable electrodeposited gold, colour stability that comes from purity rather than from a hardener and therefore drifts less, and an electrolyte that does not attack steel the way an acid citrate bath does, which makes an accidental bare-metal touch less catastrophic. Hardened variants exist but generally sit at or below hardened acid gold, and the arsenic- or thallium-class dopants some of them use re-import the hazmat burden the family was chosen to escape.

included: the complex-stability mechanism and the disproportionation problem it creates
what cyanide-free status does and does not buy
ductility, low stress and purity-based colour stability
the hardened-variant trade and its dopant classes
excluded: stabiliser dosing and free-sulfite control in service
bath death economics, reclaim and recovery
setpoints of any kind

pros.claim: It gives a small bench a real gold-plating capability without the cyanide obligation class
pros.example: a studio that could never satisfy secure segregated cyanide storage can still plate honest micron-class gold on prepared work

cons.claim: Shorter bath life and much tighter drag-in sensitivity make it the more expensive chemistry per useful hour despite the cheaper compliance
cons.example: an acid drag-in that a cyanide bath would shrug off can crash a sulfite bath and precipitate its gold onto the tank wall

failure_modes: treating cyanide-free as hazard-free and relaxing storage, labelling or waste discipline
selecting a doped hardened variant and quietly reacquiring the hazmat duties the family was chosen to avoid
expecting cyanide-grade bath life and building a schedule on it
acceptance_tests: a cyanide-free selection states whether a hardened variant is involved and what its dopant class implies, and records the bath-life expectation the schedule is built on
revisit_triggers: bath life falls short of the expectation the selection assumed
the job's wear class rises beyond what an undoped soft deposit supports

base.update_signal: supplier or corpus evidence revising cyanide-free bath life, hardness ceilings or stabiliser behaviour

nodes.definition: The class with no rectifier, holding two very different mechanisms. Immersion or displacement gold uses the part's own surface metal as the reducing agent, so it stops as soon as gold covers the surface — a self-limiting flash with a hard ceiling the corpus places around a tenth of a micron, which is a colour coat and nothing more. Autocatalytic electroless gold uses a reducing agent in the bath and can genuinely build, but it is the slowest and fussiest gold per micron in the catalogue. Both usually ride on electroless nickel-phosphorus, whose defining virtue is perfectly uniform thickness on any geometry — bores, hollows, chain and filigree — where rack plating's current distribution simply fails, and whose defining vice is that the nickel-phosphorus layer is hard and close to brittle, which makes the whole stack the worst possible choice for anything bent after coating. On a jewellery bench the class earns its place in three honest roles: metallising non-conductors so they can then be electroplated, laying a uniform barrier and gold seed on complex formed pieces, and supplying a flash tier that is sold as a flash tier.

included: the displacement and autocatalytic mechanisms and the self-limiting ceiling
electroless nickel-phosphorus as underlayer, its uniformity and its brittleness
metallisation of non-conductors as the front-end route
the three honest bench roles for the class
excluded: electroless bath control, activator ageing and replenishment
sensitising and activating procedure detail
vacuum coating alternatives

pros.claim: It reaches geometry no rack can throw into, with no rectifier and no current distribution problem at all
pros.example: a hollow filigree pendant coats uniformly inside and out where a rack gold bath leaves the recesses visibly pale

cons.claim: The displacement ceiling is physics rather than a tuning problem, and the nickel-phosphorus underlayer forbids any post-coating forming
cons.example: selling an immersion-gold ring as durable plate produces a return, because no amount of extra time in the tank puts more gold on a surface that has stopped reacting

failure_modes: describing an immersion flash with a plated-coating claim it cannot physically meet
bending or sizing a part that carries a nickel-phosphorus stack
expecting autocatalytic build to be economic at jewellery volumes
acceptance_tests: a selection in this class states which of the three roles it is being used for and, where immersion gold is involved, records the flash-class ceiling and the claim class that follows from it
revisit_triggers: the job acquires a forming, sizing or setting step after coating
the customer's durability expectation rises above the flash class

base.update_signal: corpus or supplier evidence changing the practical thickness ceiling or the economics of autocatalytic build

nodes.definition: A strike is not a thin version of the build bath; it is a different bath doing a different job. It is deliberately lean in gold and rich in complexant so that a less-noble surface cannot spontaneously displace gold out of solution — the immersion deposit that is the root cause of adhesion failure in strike-less gold plating — and it is run to grip rather than to build. It is also sacrificial by design: sitting first in the sequence, it collects the drag-in that would otherwise poison a far more valuable build bath, which is why the correct response to a contaminated strike is to remake it rather than to nurse it. Live entry, meaning current on before the work enters the solution, belongs to this step. The selection consequences are direct: the strike must belong to the same supplier system as the build bath unless both sheets say otherwise, and a family whose strike is weak is a poor choice for difficult, passive or mixed-metal surfaces.

included: why a strike exists: immersion suppression and adhesion
its sacrificial role protecting the build bath
live entry as part of the step
system compatibility between strike and build
excluded: strike setpoints and titration
when to dump it and how its gold is recovered
the cleaning and activation that precede it

pros.claim: A correct strike turns a marginal adhesion job into a routine one while protecting the shop's most valuable solution
pros.example: a cyanide strike's activation strength is what makes gold stay on awkward mixed-metal joints that a build bath alone would release within days

cons.claim: It is another tank with its own analysis, its own gold inventory and its own drag-out path
cons.example: a small bench adding a strike now has two gold solutions to keep alive, analysed and segregated rather than one

failure_modes: skipping the strike to save a tank and then blaming the peeling on cleaning
trying to save a contaminated strike by dosing it instead of remaking it
entering the strike without current so an immersion deposit forms in the first seconds
acceptance_tests: the plan names a strike that belongs to the same supplier system as the build bath, states the live-entry requirement, and records the remake-rather-than-rescue rule for the strike
revisit_triggers: adhesion failures appear at the gold interface rather than at the underplate
the build bath family changes and the strike no longer matches it

base.update_signal: supplier guidance on strike compatibility, or repeated adhesion failures traced to the strike step

nodes.definition: Decide how many gold baths this finish actually needs and what each one is for. Three roles exist and they are not interchangeable: the strike grips and protects, the build carries thickness and therefore wear life, and a colour or flash bath puts the final hue on last as a thin decorative coat. A job may need one role, two or all three — a heavy-wear item in a plain fine-gold tone may need strike plus build, a rose tone over a durable base needs strike, build and colour, and an honestly-sold flash tier may need only one bath. The architecture also has to fit the room it lives in: every bath is a tank, a heater, an analysis regime, a drag-out path and a standing gold inventory, and its physical position has to respect the segregation rules, keeping cyanide-bearing and acid tanks apart with their own trays and drains. Choosing the architecture is where a selection stops being a chemistry preference and becomes a commitment the shop has to sustain.

included: assigning the three bath roles to a specific job
deciding how many gold tanks the finish requires
layout consequences for tank, tray and drain segregation
excluded: rack and barrel choice and run sequencing
each bath's in-service control regime
waste treatment routing

pros.claim: Separating the roles lets each bath be good at one thing instead of mediocre at three
pros.example: a thin alloyed colour flash over a thicker plain build gives the wear life of the build together with the hue of the flash, which neither bath delivers alone

cons.claim: Every added role multiplies the standing cost of simply being ready to plate
cons.example: three gold tanks means three inventories, three analysis routines and three drag-out streams for a shop that may only plate twice a week

failure_modes: using a colour flash as if it were the wear layer
running strike and build out of one tank to save space
laying tanks out for walking convenience and breaking the acid and cyanide separation
acceptance_tests: every gold tank in the plan has one stated role, a named product, and a position in the layout that satisfies the segregation rule from the readiness verdict
revisit_triggers: a new colour or wear class is added to the product range
the room, its ventilation or its drainage layout changes

base.update_signal: a change in the product range or in the room that makes the current tank architecture unsustainable

nodes.definition: Understand hue as a composition question rather than a knob. A pure gold bath gives one colour, the rich 24k-class yellow, and every other tone is achieved by co-depositing another metal: the corpus records copper additions driving the deposit pink and rose, nickel paling it toward a green-white, and silver pushing it green, while in the hardened acid family the cobalt or nickel hardener shifts tone slightly rose or slightly paler and greener as a side effect of its real job. Because the coating is then an alloy, its effective karat is below 24 and is a property of the recipe, which is why the honest statement to a customer is a colour class plus a coating description rather than a karat number borrowed from solid-gold language. Two mechanisms therefore compete at selection: colour by alloy addition, which is tunable but drifts as the additions and conditions drift, and colour by purity, which is stable but offers exactly one hue.

included: which co-deposited metals shift hue in which direction
hardener-driven tone shift as a side effect
effective karat of a coating as a recipe property
colour-by-alloy versus colour-by-purity as a stability trade
excluded: analysing and holding alloy additions in service
measuring deposit composition
karat marking and claim wording

pros.claim: It makes colour a designed property instead of a lucky one
pros.example: a customer's rose target points squarely at a copper-bearing colour bath rather than at somebody trying to run the yellow bath differently

cons.claim: Every hue-shifting addition is one more thing that drifts, and drift shows up first as colour
cons.example: a rose flash that creeps steadily more orange batch after batch because the addition and the operating conditions moved together

failure_modes: describing an alloyed coating with solid-gold karat language
chasing a colour by improvising additions instead of selecting the product's colour bath
overlooking that a nickel-bearing hue is also a skin-contact question
acceptance_tests: the colour route is recorded as either alloy-based or purity-based, with the co-deposited metal named where one is involved, and the customer-facing description avoids solid-gold karat language
revisit_triggers: the colour target changes or a second tone is added to the range
colour drift appears in a hue that depends on an alloy addition

base.update_signal: supplier colour-bath documentation or shop colour records that revise which additions deliver which tone reliably

nodes.definition: Gold is almost never plated straight onto the customer's metal, so choosing the support baths is part of choosing the gold system. Nickel is the workhorse underplate and arrives in classes with different jobs: a bright levelling nickel supplies the mirror that reads straight through a thin gold layer, which is the classic way a modest gold thickness looks expensive, while a low-stress sulfamate-class nickel is the ductile choice whenever the part will be formed, because brighteners embrittle the deposit. A copper strike or a levelling copper is the traditional answer on mild steel and zinc die-cast. A palladium or palladium-nickel class serves as the barrier where nickel is unwanted. Passive stainless takes a Wood's-class nickel strike or nothing adheres to it at all. The barrier's jobs are concrete and worth naming: block base-metal diffusion into thin gold, block corrosion through the coating's pores, and level the surface so the gold behaves and looks like more than it is.

included: nickel classes and what bright versus sulfamate each buys
copper strike and levelling copper as a class
palladium-class barriers as the nickel alternative
Wood's-class strike for passive stainless
the barrier's diffusion, pore and levelling jobs
excluded: nickel and copper bath control and analysis
surface preparation before the underplate
nickel-release compliance, which has its own unit

pros.claim: The underplate is the single biggest lever on both wear life and appearance under a thin gold coat
pros.example: a couple of microns of levelled bright nickel makes a modest gold thickness look and wear far better than the same gold laid on a dull, unlevelled substrate

cons.claim: It is a second full plating line with its own tanks, chemistry, control and waste stream
cons.example: taking on steel substrates roughly doubles the wet line before a single gram of gold has been deposited on anything

failure_modes: choosing a brightener-bearing nickel under a part that will be formed
skipping the Wood's-class strike on passive stainless and blaming the gold bath for the peeling
treating palladium as a drop-in swap for nickel without re-qualifying colour and adhesion
acceptance_tests: the underplate is specified by class, by ductility requirement and by thickness class with the product sheet referenced, and skin-contact items carry the nickel-release check before the class is fixed
revisit_triggers: the forming order changes, making ductility of the underplate decisive
the item becomes skin-contact or its target market changes
adhesion or corrosion failures appear at the barrier rather than in the gold

base.update_signal: supplier or corpus evidence revising which underplate class suits which forming and appearance requirement

nodes.definition: When the finished item is worn against skin, the default nickel barrier stops being a purely technical choice and becomes a regulatory and ethical one. Nickel-release limits for skin-contact jewellery exist as an obligation class with named test standards and regulations in several markets; the specific limits, the test methods and which markets they bind are exactly the sort of thing to verify currently in your own jurisdiction rather than to quote from memory or from a supplier's marketing. The selection consequences are concrete: either keep nickel out of the stack by using a palladium-class or other non-nickel barrier, or keep it under a coating whose integrity you can actually defend and evidence, remembering that a cracked, thin or porous gold layer exposes whatever sits beneath it. This unit is educational only — a customer's allergy question belongs with their clinician, and a compliance question belongs with current local rules and, where the market demands it, with a testing service.

included: nickel release as an obligation class to verify locally and currently
non-nickel barrier options as classes
the link between coating integrity, porosity and exposure
routing allergy and compliance questions to clinicians, rules and testing services
excluded: any asserted release limit, threshold or test result
medical advice of any kind
the test procedure itself

pros.claim: It catches a compliance and comfort failure while it is still only a barrier choice
pros.example: an earring line destined for a market with release rules gets re-stacked once at selection instead of being recalled after it has shipped

cons.claim: Nickel-free stacks generally cost more and behave differently, so the swap is never free
cons.example: a palladium-class barrier changes both the cost and the tone that reads through a thin gold layer, which forces the colour qualification to be repeated

failure_modes: quoting a numeric release limit as settled fact
assuming any gold layer makes the nickel underneath irrelevant regardless of thickness or porosity
offering a customer medical reassurance instead of a referral
acceptance_tests: for every skin-contact item the record states the barrier class chosen, the jurisdiction whose rules were checked, the date of that check, and the testing route if the market requires evidence
revisit_triggers: the target market changes or its rules are revised
the item's contact status changes from non-contact to skin-contact
a customer raises a sensitivity concern on a delivered line

base.update_signal: a change in the target market's nickel-release rules or test standards, or new supplier evidence on non-nickel barrier performance

nodes.definition: Match the bath system to the metal actually under it, in both directions: what the substrate does to the deposit, and what the electrolyte does to the substrate. The corpus's hard rules travel with every family. Gold is never plated directly onto bare steel, because iron displaces gold out of solution into a zero-adhesion immersion deposit and then contaminates the bath with dissolved iron. Passive stainless adheres to nothing without a Wood's-class nickel strike to break its oxide film. Copper and brass need a barrier because copper diffuses into thin gold and dulls it. Silver takes the vermeil-class route with a barrier against migration. Zinc die-cast needs its own strike before anything else. Non-conductors cannot be electroplated at all until they have been metallised. The reverse direction matters just as much and is often forgotten: an acid gold electrolyte chemically attacks bare steel while an alkaline sulfite bath does not, which changes how catastrophic an accidental bare-metal touch turns out to be.

included: substrate classes and the stack each demands
immersion deposition and interdiffusion as failure mechanisms
the electrolyte-attacks-substrate direction
routing non-conductors to metallisation before any electroplating
excluded: cleaning, pickling and activation execution
alloy identification testing methods
any setpoint or immersion time

pros.claim: It catches the failures that no amount of good bath control can rescue afterwards
pros.example: a stainless clasp plated without a Wood's-class strike peels regardless of how perfectly the gold bath is running

cons.claim: Substrate identity is often uncertain on customer work, and the safe stack is the expensive one
cons.example: an unmarked white metal has to be treated as the worst case, adding a strike and a barrier the job might not actually have needed

failure_modes: trusting a customer's description of the metal without verification
ignoring solder alloys and previous plated repairs hiding under the surface
letting an acid bath contact exposed steel through a gap in the barrier
acceptance_tests: the plan states the substrate class, the required strike and barrier for it, and confirms that no path exists in which a gold or acid electrolyte contacts bare base metal
revisit_triggers: substrate verification contradicts the intake assumption
adhesion or staining failures appear that point at the substrate rather than the bath

base.update_signal: a substrate class the shop has not handled before, or corpus evidence revising a stack requirement

nodes.definition: Decide when the metal gets bent relative to when the gold goes on, because that single decision eliminates whole families. Hardened acid gold is brittle — the corpus records elongation well under one percent against several percent for soft gold — so bending after plating microcracks it and opens both the barrier and the base metal to corrosion and to skin exposure. Soft alkaline cyanide gold is the most ductile electrodeposited gold; undoped sulfite gold is close behind and low in stress; electroless nickel-phosphorus is the worst of all, cracking through its thickness and taking the gold with it. The underplate matters as much as the gold, because brightener-bearing nickel embrittles while a sulfamate-class nickel keeps the stack formable. Even the best stack crazes at a tight enough radius, so the default production answer is form first and plate afterwards; plate-then-form is a deliberate choice that buys forming freedom by spending wear resistance, and it has to be disclosed rather than discovered.

included: family-by-family formability ranking
the underplate's contribution to stack ductility
bend radius as a limit on any stack
the wear-resistance price of plate-then-form
excluded: forming technique, tooling and radius design
heat treatment procedures
post-form inspection methods

pros.claim: One early question removes the most expensive category of rework a plating bench sees
pros.example: learning at intake that the clips are bent after plating rules out hardened gold before any chemistry is ordered, rather than after a hundred pieces have crazed

cons.claim: Form-first constrains production flow and makes handling harder
cons.example: finished delicate forms are fiddlier to rack, easier to damage in the tank and slower to load than flat stock would be

failure_modes: bending a hardened-gold part gently and then calling the crazing a bath problem
assuming warmth or annealing makes a brittle deposit formable
specifying a bright levelling nickel under a part that will be formed
acceptance_tests: the forming order is stated explicitly in the selection, the family shortlist is filtered by it, and any plate-then-form decision records the wear-resistance trade and the disclosure that accompanies it
revisit_triggers: the design acquires or removes a post-plate forming, sizing or setting step
cracking or flaking appears at bend radii in production

base.update_signal: production evidence of cracking at radii the current family and underplate were expected to survive

nodes.definition: Two physical properties decide how a family behaves as a production process rather than as a finish: how much of the current actually becomes gold, and how evenly the deposit reaches the awkward parts of the piece. The corpus records the alkaline cyanide family at very high cathode efficiency and the hardened acid family far lower, which is why the same target thickness takes markedly longer in the hard-gold tank at comparable current — the electricity is trivial, but bench time and rack occupancy are not. Throwing power decides whether recesses, bores and the insides of hollow forms receive anything at all, and where it runs out, more current burns edges rather than filling recesses, so the answer is a different process class instead of a bigger rectifier. Treat published efficiency figures as handbook-class comparisons that set expectations; the product's own sheet and the shop's own logged runs are what calibrate the real time per micron on this bench with these racks.

included: cathode efficiency as a family-level selection axis
throwing power and geometry limits
time per micron and rack occupancy as real production costs
handbook figures treated as calibration-worthy expectations
excluded: calculating current and time for a specific rack
measuring achieved thickness
efficiency change as a bath-health signal in service

pros.claim: It turns the question of which bath into a schedulable production answer
pros.example: a heavy-wear batch can be quoted with an honest turnaround once the slower hardened family's time per micron is understood rather than assumed

cons.claim: Both properties are geometry- and setup-dependent, so family-level figures are only a starting expectation
cons.example: a densely loaded rack of small parts behaves nothing like the flat coupon the expectation was built on, and the difference shows up as thin recesses

failure_modes: promising a turnaround based on the fast family's efficiency while actually running the slow one
raising current to fix a throwing-power problem and burning the edges instead
quoting handbook efficiency as if it were this bench's measured rate
acceptance_tests: the plan records an expected time per micron for the chosen family and geometry, marked as an expectation to be calibrated against the shop's own logged runs
revisit_triggers: actual run times diverge persistently from the expectation
a new geometry class enters the product range

base.update_signal: logged run data from this bench that replaces the handbook-class expectation with a measured rate

nodes.definition: Every gold bath the shop decides to own is gold it has already bought and cannot sell until it is recovered: the metal standing in a tank is its volume multiplied by its gold concentration, so a bench with a strike, a build and a colour bath carries three inventories sitting idle between jobs, along with three analysis regimes and three drag-out paths. Families differ in how long that investment stays usable — the corpus records cyanide baths as long-lived and forgiving while sulfite baths die in fewer metal turnovers — and at small volumes drag-out can carry away more gold than the parts actually receive unless a static drag-out rinse returns solution to the tank. The decision this drives is unglamorous and decisive: how many gold systems can this bench genuinely keep alive, analysed and honest? One well-maintained family almost always beats three neglected ones, and neglect shows up as a deposit nobody can explain.

included: gold as standing inventory expressed as volume times concentration
per-family bath-life expectations as qualitative classes
drag-out as a loss path that influences the selection
how many gold systems the bench can sustain
excluded: prices, gold market values and any monetary figure
recovery and refining of spent solution and rinses
replenishment scheduling and dosing

pros.claim: It exposes the standing cost of capability, which is what actually sinks small plating benches
pros.example: a second gold family added for one customer's tone quietly halves the maintenance attention the first family receives, and both baths get worse

cons.claim: The same discipline can under-serve genuine variety and push every job into one bath
cons.example: forcing a rose request into the existing yellow line produces a compromise colour the customer never asked for and did not agree to

failure_modes: counting only the gold that lands on parts and ignoring the gold standing in tanks
adding families without adding the maintenance capacity to keep them analysed
letting an idle bath age unanalysed because it is not currently in use
acceptance_tests: the plan records the standing gold inventory per tank as volume times concentration, the bath-life expectation for each family, and who analyses and maintains each tank
revisit_triggers: a new family or colour bath is proposed for the bench
maintenance attention per tank falls below what the plan assumed

base.update_signal: the shop's own records of bath life and drag-out loss replacing the family-level expectation

nodes.definition: The words attached to the finished piece are part of the selection, not an afterthought for the label printer. Gold plated, vermeil, gold filled and rolled gold are distinct claim classes with distinct requirements — some describe an electroplated coating over a specified substrate at a specified minimum thickness class, while others describe a mechanically bonded layer that is not electroplating at all — and the exact definitions and thresholds are set by the market's rules and must be verified currently in your jurisdiction rather than recalled from a supplier's catalogue. Selection therefore has to be able to support the claim the shop intends to make: a vermeil-class claim constrains both the substrate and the coating thickness class, and an immersion-gold flash cannot carry a plated-coating claim its physics forbids. Underneath all of it sits the non-negotiable rule of this trade: a plated piece is never represented as solid gold, and the wear expectation is disclosed before the sale rather than after the complaint.

included: the claim terms as obligation classes to verify locally and currently
the constraint a claim places back on substrate and thickness class
wear-expectation disclosure before sale
the rule that plated work is never described as solid gold
excluded: asserted numeric thickness thresholds or legal definitions
hallmarking and assay procedure
pricing and marketing copywriting

pros.claim: Aligning the claim with the physics prevents a compliance problem and a broken customer relationship at the same time
pros.example: an honestly labelled flash tier sells steadily and returns rarely, while the identical coating sold as durable plate does the opposite

cons.claim: The honest class is often the less saleable one and the pressure to blur it is constant
cons.example: a wholesale buyer asking for the word vermeil on a base-metal item that cannot carry the claim under any reading of the rules

failure_modes: quoting a thickness threshold for a claim class from memory
using the word gold in copy without the coating qualifier that makes it true
disclosing wear expectations only once the returns conversation has started
acceptance_tests: the intended claim class is named before production, the jurisdiction whose rules were checked and the date of the check are recorded, and the selected stack is confirmed capable of supporting that claim
revisit_triggers: the target market changes or its marking rules are revised
the coating class actually achieved differs from what the claim assumed

base.update_signal: a change in a target market's marking or claim rules, or a regulator publication clarifying a class

nodes.definition: Some jobs are not wet-plating jobs at all, and knowing where that boundary lies is part of being useful rather than a confession of weakness. Physical vapour deposition is a vacuum coating class with a different capital base, a different palette that includes the hard ceramic-toned finishes no gold bath produces, and a natural fit for glass and for very hard thin decorative coatings. This knowledge base names it only as an alternative class for referral: it does not specify, select, price or compare vacuum coating work beyond that class-level statement. The bench-level decision is a triage: when the requirement is a hard ceramic-class tone, a substrate the wet line genuinely cannot serve, or a durability expectation that electroplated gold at a jewellery-sensible thickness cannot meet, say so, refer the work, and do not accept it as a plating job that will disappoint. The same triage refuses work the shop's hazard readiness or substrate capability cannot honestly serve.

included: naming vacuum coating as an out-of-scope alternative class
the triage that produces a referral or an honest refusal
refusal on readiness or capability grounds as a legitimate outcome
excluded: any vacuum coating process, equipment or parameter detail
performance comparisons beyond class level
recommending or vetting a specific vendor

pros.claim: It protects both the customer and the shop from a job the wet line was never going to win
pros.example: a request for a hard dark ceramic-class tone is referred out rather than attempted with a gold bath and a hopeful topcoat

cons.claim: Referral loses revenue and can read to the customer as incapacity
cons.example: a customer hears that the shop cannot do one finish and quietly moves the whole account elsewhere

failure_modes: accepting an out-of-class job and over-promising to keep the customer
treating vacuum coating as a rival to be argued against rather than a different tool
implying an electroplated flash is equivalent to a vacuum hard coating
acceptance_tests: jobs that fall outside the wet line are recorded with the reason for referral or refusal and the alternative class the customer was pointed toward
revisit_triggers: the shop acquires a capability that moves the boundary
a repeated referral pattern suggests a real gap in the service offering

base.update_signal: a change in the shop's capability set, or a pattern of referrals revealing a gap worth closing

nodes.definition: Prove the chosen system on something that is not the customer's piece. Plate coupons or sacrificial pieces of the same substrate, prepared through the same route and racked in the worst geometry the job contains, then check the four things a selection can get wrong: does the coating stick, does it match the agreed colour reference under the agreed viewing conditions, does it reach the recesses the design contains, and does it survive the handling or forming the design demands. Deposit thickness and composition checks belong to the quality specialist's method classes — a plated coupon read on an X-ray fluorescence instrument is the usual route — and this step consumes that result rather than redefining it. The gate is binary and unpopular under deadline: no customer work enters an unqualified system, because stripping and replating a finished piece costs more than a coupon in every currency, including the customer's trust.

included: coupon design mirroring substrate, preparation route and worst geometry
the four selection-level checks: adhesion, colour, coverage and handling survival
consuming quality-specialist method-class results
the binary go or no-go gate
excluded: the test methods and acceptance criteria themselves
in-service bath monitoring
customer sign-off on the finished piece

pros.claim: It converts a paper selection into evidence at the cheapest moment it will ever be available
pros.example: a coupon reveals pale recesses on a filigree form while the customer's pendant is still sitting untouched in the drawer

cons.claim: Coupons consume gold, time and bench capacity before any revenue arrives
cons.example: a small shop against a deadline is tempted to qualify on the customer's own piece and usually regrets exactly that decision

failure_modes: qualifying on flat stock when the job is hollow or deeply recessed
comparing colour under different light than the agreed viewing condition
treating a passed coupon as permanent rather than as a snapshot of that bath on that day
acceptance_tests: a dated coupon set exists on the job's substrate and worst geometry with recorded adhesion, colour-versus-reference, coverage and handling results, and no customer work is released into the system until all four pass
revisit_triggers: any coupon check fails or is marginal
the bath, the product revision or the preparation route changes after qualification

base.update_signal: coupon results that contradict what the family and stack were expected to deliver

nodes.definition: Close the selection by writing it down in a form the next run and the bath-maintenance side can actually use: the job profile it answers, the family chosen and the named commercial product with its sheet on file, the strike, build and colour architecture with the support baths beneath it, the hazard readiness verdict that permitted the choice, the claim class the finish can honestly carry, the qualification coupon evidence, and the residual risks that were accepted rather than solved. This is the handoff artifact — bath control, drift signatures and replenishment discipline live in the maintenance knowledge base, and that work needs to know what was selected and why in order to defend it against a drifting result. Also record what was rejected and for what reason, because the rejected options are what a future operator will otherwise rediscover the expensive way. An unwritten selection decays into folklore within a few runs, and folklore is what produces the batch nobody can explain.

included: the required contents of the selection record
rejected alternatives and the reason each was rejected
accepted residual risks
the handoff into bath maintenance
excluded: the bath log and its in-service control entries
quality records and certificates
customer-facing quotations

pros.claim: It makes the next identical job a repeat instead of a rediscovery
pros.example: a returning customer's rose flash is reproduced from the dossier rather than re-derived from three people's partial memories

cons.claim: Documentation is the first thing dropped when the bench is busy, so the record decays exactly when it is most needed
cons.example: a rush job selected verbally leaves no trace at all when the same customer returns a year later asking for more of the same

failure_modes: recording the chosen option but never the rejected ones or the reasons
omitting the residual risks so they resurface later as surprises
letting the dossier go stale after a product reformulation or a rule change
acceptance_tests: the dossier names the job profile, family, product and sheet revision, the full bath and support architecture, the readiness verdict, the claim class, the coupon evidence, the rejected alternatives and the accepted residual risks, and is handed to the bath-maintenance side before production starts
revisit_triggers: the product is reformulated, renamed or discontinued
a rule, market or customer requirement in the dossier changes
a repeat order arrives and the dossier no longer matches what the bench runs

base.update_signal: a reformulation, rule change or repeat order that the existing dossier no longer describes correctly

edges.why_related: the wear class is derived from the service duty the intake profile captured
the family is only selectable as a named commercial product whose sheet governs its window and its matching components
hardener level, window and compatible strike for a hardened acid gold come from the product sheet, not from the family description
the family cannot be shortlisted until the readiness verdict says the shop may run cyanide-bearing chemistry
the near-neutral class is understood as the compatibility answer to the acid family's pH, so it is defined relative to it
the strike role is defined family by family, and this family supplies the strongest strikes in the catalogue
the architecture cannot be laid out until the strike's role and its system compatibility are understood
how much build thickness the architecture must carry follows directly from the wear class assigned
the alloying route is chosen to hit a target that must already be fixed as a reference
matching a bath system to a substrate is impossible without knowing which barrier and strike classes are available to bridge them
non-conductors and unreachable geometry are only platable through the metallisation route this class supplies
the nickel-release question only becomes actionable once the barrier classes and their alternatives are on the table
the forming decision is framed by the brittleness of the hardened deposit more than by any other family property
the family's markedly lower cathode efficiency is the anchor case for reasoning about time per micron
how long a tank is occupied per job feeds directly into how many systems the bench can sustain
the coupon has to be cut from the same substrate class the compatibility analysis assumed, or it proves nothing
the dossier records the coupon evidence, so the qualification must be complete before it can be written
the referral triage runs against the requirement profile the intake captured
going cyanide-free removes one obligation class but the readiness verdict still binds, because arsenic- or thallium-class dopants in hardened variants reintroduce serious hazmat duties
a skin-contact obligation removes the default nickel barrier from the stack, so the substrate bridging plan has to be rebuilt around a palladium-class or other alternative
the claim the shop intends to make sets a floor on substrate and thickness class, which the bath architecture must be built to reach
a heavy-wear class pushes the family choice toward a hardened deposit and rules out an unhardened soft coat as the final surface
a plate-then-form requirement eliminates nickel-phosphorus stacks outright, because the underlayer cracks through its thickness and takes the gold with it
how many tanks the bench can genuinely keep analysed and alive caps how many gold roles the architecture is allowed to use
the hardness that buys wear life is exactly what makes the deposit crack when the part is formed afterwards
edges.resolution_rule: form first and plate afterwards by default; if the design fixes plate-then-form, drop to a ductile soft-gold family, accept and disclose the lower scratch resistance, and never promise both properties on the same piece

edges.why_related: the family that is technically best for ductile, rich-coloured work is also the one carrying the heaviest obligation class
edges.resolution_rule: the readiness verdict wins without exception: a shop that cannot satisfy training, segregation, storage, ventilation and emergency readiness does not run the family, and the job moves to an alternative family or goes out to a shop that can

edges.why_related: the cyanide-free family's ductile high-purity deposit is soft, which collides with a heavy-wear requirement
edges.resolution_rule: the wear class wins for daily-wear items: either compensate with thickness class and a hard final layer applied after forming, or restrict the family to lower wear classes and disclose the expectation in writing before the sale

edges.why_related: the self-limiting thickness ceiling of immersion gold collides with the plated-coating claim a seller would prefer to make
edges.resolution_rule: physics wins over vocabulary: sell an immersion coat as the flash class it is, or move to an electroplated build that can actually reach the thickness class the claim requires

edges.why_related: nickel is both a hue-shifting alloy addition and a hardener, and it is exactly the metal a skin-contact obligation wants out of the stack
edges.resolution_rule: for skin-contact items the nickel-release obligation class wins: reach the hue through copper- or silver-class additions or a different family, keep nickel out of the exposed layers, and verify the current rules of the target market

edges.why_related: qualification consumes gold, tank time and bench capacity before any revenue, which is precisely what an inventory-conscious shop wants to conserve
edges.resolution_rule: qualification wins ahead of every customer piece: coupons are cheaper than stripping and replating finished work, and the gold in a coupon is recoverable while a damaged heirloom is not

edges.why_related: the lean alloyed flash variants of this family are what physically produce tuned hues, because co-deposited copper, nickel or silver shifts the deposit rose, pale or green

because hardener level and operating conditions jointly set the tone of a hardened deposit, choosing this family causes batch-to-batch colour variation that only a plated coupon against the reference exposes
brightener-bearing nickel embrittles and cracks first when a plated part is bent, so the underplate class chosen is what actually causes the stack's forming limit
having no current distribution at all is what gives this class uniform coverage in bores and filigree, and the self-limiting displacement reaction is what caps its rate and thickness
the colour reference and its viewing conditions have to be agreed before coupons are plated, otherwise the coupon has nothing to be judged against
the barrier decision and its jurisdiction check must be settled before any claim or customer-facing description of the finish is written
coupon results that miss colour, coverage or adhesion send the decision back to the family and product choice rather than to a parameter tweak
residual risks recorded in the dossier often re-open the job profile, forcing a wear class, colour target or claim to be renegotiated with the customer
both deposit a soft, high-purity, ductile 24k-class gold and therefore compete for the same formable and rich-colour jobs, while differing completely in hazard class and bath life

conflict_axes.name: wear_hardness_versus_formability
